fixes: Set tariff.VERSION and the pyproject version to the manifest version 2.4.1, the requires-python to >=3.12 and the dependencies to an empty list, dropping the third-party requests requirement.
Made tier 1 cover the units up to and including its up_to, instead of stopping one unit short of it.
Tiered a meter's units by their account position, offsetting each meter by the period quantity of the account's earlier meters in ascending meter order.
Prorated the standing charge over each calendar month the meter is active in, by that month's own length, instead of a flat 30-day month.
Added the missing outside_period exception and kept the reason order malformed_quantity, unknown_meter, inactive_meter, outside_period, duplicate_read.
Rejected text, decimal, boolean and negative quantities as malformed_quantity, since only a JSON integer of 0 or more is a quantity.
Read the account allowance from billing_periods.csv and shared it in equal parts over the account's energy lines, re-sharing whatever stays unshared among the lines not yet at zero.

Based the commitment credit on the invoice subtotal, computing the total as subtotal x (1 - credit_rate) and the credit as subtotal minus total, instead of rating raw unaccepted quantities into a separate base.
Computed every amount from the decimal values as written in the inputs with exact fractions, rounded half to even to 0.01, and wrote each amount as a two-decimal JSON string.
Sorted the exception list by read_id alone, not by account and read_id.
Made python -m tariff report `missing input: <file name>` on standard error and exit 2 for the first missing input file, printing nothing.
Corrected the README, which described a flat 30-day proration and a credit on metered consumption.
Corrected test_partial_period_standing_charge and test_commitment_credit_base, whose expected amounts followed the drifted behaviour.
